scripts/lwb_check_env_leak.py was NOT run as proof: it reports UNCONFIGURED in this environment because LWB_PRIVATE_NEEDLES (a repo secret) is unset locally, and a clean UNCONFIGURED result proves nothing. It runs for real only in CI.

scripts/lwb_lanes.py was checked locally with `--base origin/main --head HEAD` and reported no violating paths, but was NOT run with `--pr-number 51` (the real enforcement mode, which also checks reviews/51/ for independent-review records) since this PR number did not exist yet when most of the verification commands ran; CI runs the real check.
All commands were run on Linux only, in this one container. CI runs the same suite across ubuntu/macos/windows and Python 3.10/3.12; that six-way matrix was not independently reproduced here.

The two 'decide and document' design choices (leaving the detached-HEAD-no-PR-number case and engine.py's rule-crash fail-open out of scope) are judgement calls, not something a command can prove correct. The tests above prove the CURRENT behavior matches what was decided; they do not prove the decision itself is the right one -- that is exactly what independent review under reviews/51/ is for, and the reasoning is stated in full in this PR's own description for a reviewer to attack.

`scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --reexecute` was NOT run against this record as part of writing it (a record cannot contain proof of its own existence or its own re-execution, per proof/README.md) and was not separately run against the wider proof/ corpus in this session either.

python scripts/lwb_check_commit_identity.py was run with explicit --base/--head flags scoped to this branch's own single commit; it was NOT run with no arguments (its default, which CI's own workflow step actually invokes and which scans up to the last 500 commits reachable from HEAD).
